title: Filter out null or empty employee names from the list.
shortTitle: Filter out null or empty employee names from the list
keyPoints: Two bad states to reject: null (absent reference) and blank (empty or whitespace-only string).
Test null first with short-circuit AND to avoid NullPointerException on subsequent method calls.
Java 11 isBlank() is cleaner than trim().isEmpty() for detecting whitespace-only strings.
Predicate.not(String::isBlank) is the cleanest way to filter non-blank strings in Java 11+.
Objects::nonNull filters nulls from a stream of raw references before further processing.
A reusable StringUtils.isNotBlank utility or Apache Commons provides consistent null/blank handling.
Data cleansing filters are always the first step before any business logic in banking data pipelines.

s1_definition.oneliner: Keep only names that are not null and not blank by checking non-null first (short-circuit), then non-empty, using isBlank() on Java 11+ or trim().isEmpty() on Java 8.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Null** – an absent reference; calling any method on it throws NullPointerException.
- **Blank** – an empty string or a string of only whitespace; technically a valid object but useless as a name.
- **Order** – null check must come first in the AND chain; short-circuit prevents the second check from executing on null.
- **isBlank()** – Java 11 method that returns true for empty and whitespace-only strings without explicit trim.
- **Predicate.not()** – Java 11 static method for clean negation: `filter(Predicate.not(String::isBlank))`.
s1_definition.analogy: The HR clerk at National Bank of India is cleaning the staff list before printing. Some entries have no name at all (null) and some have just empty spaces. She throws those away and keeps only the real names. That cleanup is the filter.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Null/Blank filter pipeline:
  ──────────────────────────
  Input: ["Rajesh", null, "", "   ", "Priya", null]
       │
  filter(Objects::nonNull)
       │
  ["Rajesh", "", "   ", "Priya"]
       │
  filter(Predicate.not(String::isBlank))
       │
  ["Rajesh", "Priya"]

  isBlank truth table:
  ─────────────────────
  null     → NPE (guard first!)
  ""       → true  (empty)
  "   "    → true  (whitespace only)
  "Rajesh" → false (has content)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Filtering null and blank values requires two checks in the right order: null first, then blank. Java short-circuits the AND, so the null check prevents NullPointerException on the subsequent method call. isBlank() (Java 11) handles both empty and whitespace-only strings without explicit trim.

For the cleanest syntax, use `filter(Objects::nonNull).filter(Predicate.not(String::isBlank))` which reads as 'filter: not null, then not blank.' Extract this into a reusable utility predicate because the same null/blank check appears throughout any codebase.

Data cleansing is always the first step in banking data pipelines. Before any business logic runs, remove null and blank entries so downstream code does not need defensive checks everywhere.

Remember one sentence: null check first with short-circuit, then isBlank() for empty and whitespace, and extract into a reusable utility predicate.
